To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CT441° has been expressed, purified, crystallized and the diffraction data have been collected to a resolution that is suitable for structure determination.

we have produced a protease from Chlamyida trachomatis that is important in the infection of the human host and that we have crystallized it in space group P2(1)2(1)21, with unit cell parameters a = 85.9, b = 183.9, c = 210.2 Å.
the recombinant inactive form of the protease was crystallized in a novel crystal form, and the crystal structure of this enzyme will be solved in the near future.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel chlamydial proteinase that is likely to have important roles during the infection of the human host cell.
the production and crystallization of the inactive variant CT441°, which is the first step towards the structural elucidation of this important chlamydial proteinase.
the production of a protease from C. trachoma, which has the potential to be a drug target.

the crystal structure of the inactive variant CT441° will be determined in the near future.
this is a first step in the structural elucidation of CT441°.
the CT441° crystals belong to space group P221, with unit-cell constants a = 86 Å, b = 182.8 Å, c = 210.3 Å and one molecule in the asymmetric unit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the crystal structure of CT441° has now been determined to 1.9 Å resolution (see the companion article).

we have been able to crystallize CT441°, a protease from a pathogen, in the presence of the substrate analogue Z-Gly-Pro-Arg-AMC, which is a promising step towards solving the structure of CT441° in complex with the substrate analogue.
we have been able to crystallize a variant of the chlamydial serine protease CT441 and that we have collected a diffraction data set to a resolution of ~3 Å.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CT441° crystallizes in a form suitable for structure determination by X-ray diffraction.
CT441° crystallizes in the presence of a high concentration of the substrate analogue Z-Gly-Pro-Ala-CH2Cl (1 mM) and the inhibitor Z-Phe-Phe-CH2Cl.
the production of a soluble and active protease from Chlamydiaceae, a bacterial family that is notoriously difficult to express recombinant proteins from, is possible.
